items.text: Understand what an operating system does and its role as intermediary between users and hardware
Know the history of Unix (1960s) and how Linux was born (1991)
Understand Linux layered architecture: Hardware → Kernel → Libraries → Shell → Applications
Grasp the 'everything is a file' philosophy in Linux
Know the difference between Linux kernel and GNU tools
Can navigate Linux file system using cd, pwd, and ls commands
Understand absolute vs relative paths in Linux
Know how to connect to EC2 Linux instances via EC2 Instance Connect
Can switch between standard user and root user using sudo su -
Understand the Linux file system hierarchy and purpose of key directories
Know that Linux uses single root (/) vs Windows multiple drives
Understand Linux is case-sensitive (File.txt ≠ file.txt)
Can explain difference between / (root directory) and /root (root user's home)
Know popular Linux distributions and their use cases (Amazon Linux, Ubuntu, Kali)
Understand why Linux servers use CLI instead of GUI (efficiency, automation, resources)
Can explain what Linux is and its advantages over proprietary systems
Know the difference between standard user ($) and root user (#)
Can describe the layered architecture and how commands flow through it
Understand package managers (apt vs yum) and when to use each
Can explain why case sensitivity matters in production Linux environments
Know that Amazon Linux is optimized for AWS EC2 instances
Understand EC2 Instance Connect and when to use it
Can identify which Linux AMIs are available in AWS (Amazon Linux, Ubuntu, RHEL)
Know that Amazon Linux uses yum package manager
Understand default user accounts (ec2-user for Amazon Linux, ubuntu for Ubuntu)
Comfortable navigating Linux file system
Ready to learn 25-30 essential Linux commands
Understand file permissions concept (preparing for user/group management)
Know the importance of /var/log for troubleshooting
Familiar with Linux terminal prompt and what each part means
